thread:
Maya: Quick follow-up from today's all-hands on pricing/packaging: a few concrete asks about infra/staging billing, retry token counting, and temporary quota exemptions.

Eli: can you bullet the specific questions so we can answer in-thread?

Maya: yep: 1) Are CI/staging runs charged to customer credits by default? 2) If a request automatically retries, do we charge tokens for each retry? 3) Can internal/integration tests be exempted from org monthly quotas? 4) During planned maintenance windows, does burst capacity behave differently?

Sam: TL;DR: 1) yes, billed unless using infra-scoped keys or the internal invocation flag. 2) retries are new requests, so tokens are charged per attempt. 3) yes, but must be whitelisted via ops ticket and limited to named jobs. 4) burst is subject to reserved pool caps; we don't open unlimited capacity during maintenance.

June: ops process: submit an ops ticket with org_id, CI job names, token estimate, and owner. We'll review monthly and set a whitelist entry. No open-ended org-wide exemptions.

Lisa: legal reminder: Dedicated/Private customers require contractual amendments for billing adjustments; hosted customers handled via ops policy as Sam described.

Maya: example curl for infra/internal invocations (infra keys only):
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_INFRA_KEY"
  -H "X-Redwood-Invocation-Type: internal"
  -d '{"model":"redwood-serve-small","input":"smoke test"}'
```

Sam: security note: the internal header must only be used with infra-scoped keys. Misuse by customers will auto-flag and may revoke keys. We'll add telemetry and alerts.

Eli: I'll open a docs PR with the console toggle screenshot and the exact API text, plus the ops ticket template. ETA EOW.

Maya: thanks — please ping #all-hands when PR is merged so teams see the rollout. :thumbsup:
